Does design region choice change what RFdiffusion can build?

Three contig strategies on the same input complex (crystal, 64 designs each)

Published

August 29, 2026

1 The question

Three campaign runs share an input complex, a design count and every downstream setting. They differ only in the contig string, so any difference in what RFdiffusion builds is attributable to how the design regions were chosen.

run regions designed residues how the regions were chosen
crystal_full_test_contig 2 16–26 hand-picked, two contiguous blocks
crystal_auto5A_contig 4 21–45 auto-derived from effector contact at 5 Å
crystal_auto3A_contig 6 10–19 auto-derived from effector contact at 3 Å

The posed_* runs are excluded, since they change the input structure as well as the contig. crystal_full_r1_17to21_contig is excluded because it varies only the allowed length of one region, which is the within-strategy question rather than the between-strategy one.

Everything below reads data/<run>.json, the per-run rfdiffusion_metrics.json the pipeline already writes, so nothing is recomputed from structures.

2 Where the design regions sit

Length and placement are different arguments and the summary tables only carry length, so the contig strings are drawn directly.

Code 
_ = nc.fig_contig_map()
  • The two strategies are not simply coarse and fine versions of each other. full rebuilds one large block in the middle of the domain and the C terminus, while both auto strategies scatter regions across the whole length.
  • auto 3 Å has the most regions but the fewest designed residues, because four of its six regions are one or two residues wide.

3 Displacement tracks length, but not equally between strategies

Code 
from IPython.display import Image
Image(str(nc.PLOTS / "03_com_vs_length.png"))
  • Displacement rises with region length across the pooled data, so any comparison between strategies has to account for the fact that they allow different lengths.
  • The strategies do not merely occupy different parts of that trend. full forms a tight, almost linear band, whereas both auto strategies spread widely at every length, including at one and two residues where there is very little to rebuild.

4 How much of that displacement is the scaffold moving?

Displacement is measured after aligning on the retained scaffold, so it only means “the region was rebuilt somewhere new” if the scaffold itself held still.

Code 
(designs.groupby("run", sort=False)
        .agg(designs=("design", "size"),
             median_total_designed=("total_designed", "median"),
             median_motif_rmsd=("motif_rmsd", "median"),
             median_coverage=("design_region_coverage", "median"))
        .round(3))
  • The retained scaffold barely moves under full, at a median motif RMSD of 0.07 Å, but moves 2.6 Å and 4.0 Å under auto 3 Å and auto 5 Å.
  • Part of the auto strategies’ apparent displacement is therefore the domain drifting rather than the region being rebuilt somewhere novel, so the scatter in the previous figure overstates how much extra novelty they buy.

5 Placement within a strategy

Code 
Image(str(nc.PLOTS / "01_com_displacement_by_region.png"))
Code 
(regions.groupby(["run", "region"], sort=False)
        .agg(n=("design", "size"), median_length=("length", "median"),
             median_com=("com_displacement", "median"),
             median_com_per_res=("com_per_residue", "median"))
        .round(3).reset_index())
  • Displacement varies more between regions within a strategy than it does between strategies, and the C-terminal region moves furthest in all three, at 3.7, 7.2 and 6.1 Å.
  • That region is terminal and anchored on one side only, so placement rather than length is what frees it, which is the same conclusion the per-residue column reaches for the single-residue regions of auto 3 Å.

6 Does region length change how varied the designs are?

Region 1 has a 10-20 residue allowance, so RFdiffusion picked a different length in different designs. Comparing across those lengths is free of any between-run or between-region confound, unlike the three-strategy comparison in the three-strategy comparison above.

Diversity is the mean nearest-neighbour distance between two designs’ Ca coordinates for the same region, which is defined when the two have different residue counts. Each design is compared only with designs that came out the same length. Comparing against the whole pool instead gives a spurious U, because RFdiffusion sampled lengths unevenly around 15 and the extremes then score as distant for being a minority rather than for varying among themselves.

Numbers here use the .trb-corrected residue mapping. The pipeline’s own per_region_lengths are a proportional guess, wrong for most designs of any contig with several variable-length regions. See trb_metrics.py.

Code 
from IPython.display import Image
Image("plots/11_length_vs_diversity.png")

  • Diversity rises with the length RFdiffusion built, from 0.65 Å at 10 residues to 1.14 Å at 20, or +7.0% per added residue. A quadratic term is not supported (p = 0.65), so there is no optimum length within the allowance.

  • The per-design fit gives p = 5e-07, but designs of one length share pairwise distances, so the honest test is at the length-group level. That gives rho = +0.71 over the 11 lengths, p = 0.015.

  • The C-terminal region is more varied than region 1 at any length, 2.31 Å on 6 residues, which is expected for a region anchored on one side only. The two do not overlap in length, so this is a direction rather than a matched comparison.

  • The retained scaffold held to 0.07 Å across all 64 designs, so none of the above is the fixed framework moving. All 64 designs build the same strand-loop-strand topology, so extra residues lengthen the connecting loop rather than adding elements.

7 What this supports

  • Design region choice does change what RFdiffusion builds, but region length is the weaker lever. Anchoring is the stronger one, and the clearest single comparison is the C-terminal region against interior regions of the same length.
  • Larger contiguous regions buy displacement without disturbing the retained scaffold. Fragmented regions buy displacement partly by letting the scaffold move, which is not the kind of novelty the pipeline wants.

Caveats.

  • One input complex and one effector, 64 designs per strategy. The contig strings differ in placement and in length at once, so no single comparison isolates either on its own.
  • Centre-of-mass displacement says where a region ended up, not what it looks like. Two very different backbones with the same centroid are indistinguishable here.
  • The auto strategies’ motif RMSD means their displacement is measured in a frame that itself moved, so their values are not on the same footing as full’s.
